info.title: DiCompute API
info.description: OpenAI-compatible inference API for DiCompute. Point an OpenAI SDK at the server URL below and keep your client. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`; see the authentication guide linked from `components.securitySchemes`. Note that the authenticated routes send no CORS headers and are intended for server-side clients. `429` (rate limited) is declared on every operation. An application-level limit answers in the same JSON envelope as every other error (`error.type: "rate_limit_error"`) with `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-Scope`; the same paths can also receive a 429 from an edge (Cloudflare) rule that answers `content-type: text/html` (DICOMPUTE/Open, public issue 770), so each 429 lists both media types: treat any 429 as retryable and parse its body defensively. `405` (method not allowed) is declared on every operation: calling a documented path with a method it does not declare returns 405 in the same JSON envelope as every other error (`error.type: "invalid_request_error"`, `error.code: "method_not_allowed"`) and always carries an `Allow` header (RFC 9110 s15.5.6) naming the methods that do work on that path, computed from the live route table. The `default` response of every operation is that same error envelope. The exception is the few operations that declare their own `servers` entry (the fleet gateway's public reads, served at the site origin outside `/openai`): they carry no `X-Api-Version` or `Server-Timing` header, and use the gateway's own error envelope for their `405` (also with an `Allow` header) and every other error (the same four keys, `type` not restricted to the values above); their `429` comes from the per-IP limit in front of the gateway and is `text/html` only.

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.0 for third-party apps (RFC 6749; PKCE `S256` required for public clients). Discovery: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`. The access token is an API key and is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Authorization-code and refresh-token grants are always issued the `inference` scope; the other listed scopes are enforced on API keys. Also supported at the token endpoint: `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` (ID-JAG). See the `OAuth` tag.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a retry safe: the same key and body within 24 h returns the first answer. Errors: 400 `invalid_idempotency_key`, 409 `idempotency_key_in_flight`, 422 `idempotency_key_body_mismatch` / `idempotency_key_streaming_unsupported`.

X-Api-Version.description: The API contract version. Always equal to this document's `info.version`. Sent by every operation served under `/openai`; the fleet-gateway operations (own `servers` entry) do not send it.

Server-Timing.description: One coarse metric: whole milliseconds spent inside the API from request start to response headers (`app;dur=<ms>`). For a streamed response this is time to the headers, not to the last token. Never a per-hop breakdown, and never names a worker or provider.

X-Dico-Sealed.description: `true` when the sealed-transport lane is provisioned on this deployment, `false` when it is not: the in-band signal that prompts travel readable by the infrastructure operator. Reflects the same state `GET /v1/capabilities` reports. Sent by every operation served under `/openai`; the fleet-gateway operations do not send it.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with every application-level `429` (and with a `503` that carries a capacity hint).

X-RateLimit-Scope.description: Which limiter refused the request, as a short token such as `auth_failures`. The published scope list is on the rate-limits page. Present on an application-level `429`; an edge (Cloudflare) `429` does not carry it.

X-Request-Id.description: This response's id, on every `/openai` response. Quote it to support.

X-Dico-Served-Path.description: Which path served the request: `direct` (plaintext to the engine over TLS, no worker identity, no receipt) or `fleet` (E2E-encrypted fleet dispatch).

X-Dico-Served-By.description: The serving machine's pseudonym: `worker-` followed by the first 8 hex characters of `sha256(workerId)`.

X-Dico-Confidential-Lane.description: The confidential-compute lane that served the request: `tier-0`, `tier-2` or `unverified`.

X-Dico-Worker-Trust-Level.description: The trust tier of the serving worker: `none`, `self_signed`, `pinned` or `unverified`. Present on `fleet` responses only.

X-Timing.description: A JSON object of per-stage durations in microseconds.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed per window. On an authenticated `2xx`.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the window. On an authenticated `2xx`.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the window resets. On an authenticated `2xx`.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only on a route scheduled for retirement: `@<unix-seconds>` when it was deprecated.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only on a deprecated route, always together with `Deprecation`: the HTTP-date after which the route stops answering. The replacement route is named in that operation's own description.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but not for this method (`error.type: "invalid_request_error"`, `error.code: "method_not_allowed"`). Always carries an `Allow` header (RFC 9110 s15.5.6) naming the methods that do work.

Allow.description: The comma-separated methods this path serves, from the live route table.

RateLimited.description: Rate limited. Wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry. Two layers can answer: the application limiter (`application/json`, `error.type: "rate_limit_error"`, with `X-RateLimit-Scope`) and an edge rule in front of it (`text/html`, no scope header), so parse the body defensively. The refusal contract is on the rate-limits page.

BadRequest.description: The request body failed validation (`error.type: "invalid_request_error"`) -- the same envelope every other non-2xx response on this surface uses.

Unauthorized.description: No credential was presented, or the one presented was rejected -- the same envelope every other non-2xx response on this surface uses (`error.type: "authentication_error"`). Per RFC 9110 s15.5.2 this response also always carries a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge (DICOMPUTE/Open): `Bearer realm="<deployment>"` when no credential was presented at all, or that same challenge plus `error="invalid_token"` (RFC 6750 s3.1) when one was presented and rejected.

WWW-Authenticate.description: The RFC 9110 challenge -- see this response's own description for the two forms it takes.

PaymentRequired.description: Balance or spend cap too low. Nothing ran and nothing was charged. Do not retry on a timer.

Forbidden.description: The credential is valid but may not do this: a missing scope, an organization or IP policy, or a restriction on the account.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state of the resource, for example a duplicate or an operation that is already running.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body or an uploaded file is too large for this route.

Unprocessable.description: The request is well-formed but cannot be processed, for example a value this route or model does not support.

BadGateway.description: The upstream engine or provider answered with an error.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The service cannot take the request now. Retry after `Retry-After`, if sent.

NotFound.description: No resource exists at this id (`error.type: "invalid_request_error"`) -- the same envelope every other non-2xx response on this surface uses.

GatewayMethodNotAllowed.description: A method other than GET, HEAD or OPTIONS on this path (`error.code: "method_not_allowed"`), in the gateway's envelope. Always carries an `Allow` header (RFC 9110 s15.5.6).

Allow.description: The comma-separated methods this path serves: `GET, HEAD, OPTIONS`.

EdgeRateLimited.description: Rate limited by the per-IP limit in front of the gateway. Wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry. The body is an HTML page, not the JSON envelope; `X-RateLimit-Scope` is `edge_burst`.

GatewayError.description: Error in the fleet gateway's envelope.

GeminiBadRequest.description: The request body failed validation. Gemini's error envelope, not the OpenAI one: this route speaks that protocol.

GeminiUnauthorized.description: A missing or invalid key, in Gemini's error envelope. The `WWW-Authenticate` challenge is still sent.

GeminiNotFound.description: An unknown `<model>:<action>` suffix, in Gemini's error envelope.

GeminiRateLimited.description: Rate limited. Wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry. Two layers can answer: the application limiter (`application/json`, `error.type: "rate_limit_error"`, with `X-RateLimit-Scope`) and an edge rule in front of it (`text/html`, no scope header), so parse the body defensively. The refusal contract is on the rate-limits page.

GeminiError.description: Error in Gemini's envelope. `405` comes from the shared method fallback and uses the OpenAI envelope.

kb_citations.description: Knowledge-base chunks injected into this request (`knowledge_base_id`). Absent when none were; not the web `citations`.

GeminiError.description: Gemini's error envelope, as the `/v1beta` routes send it. `code` is the HTTP status; `status` is the gRPC-style name.

warm.description: Healthy workers whose model is loaded and ready. A worker that reports no load state counts as warm.

queued_requests.description: Requests currently waiting in this model's admission queue.

queue_limit.description: The most requests that can wait in the admission queue, the same for every model. Once `queued_requests` reaches it, new requests are not queued.

token_budget_remaining.description: Tokens left in the workers' self-reported budget. Present only when at least one worker reports a budget.

token_budget_total.description: Sum of the workers' self-reported token budgets. Present only when at least one worker reports one.

estimated_ttft_ms.description: Mean estimated time to first token across healthy workers, in milliseconds. Omitted when there are too few recent samples to say.

window.description: The trailing window these numbers cover.

200.description: Run a chat completion, streaming or not. Success. When the request body sets `"stream": true`, the response is `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, not the single JSON document this section's `application/json` schema describes: a sequence of `data: <json>\n\n` frames, each JSON payload shaped like `ChatCompletionChunk` (see `components.schemas.ChatCompletionChunk`), terminated by a literal `data: [DONE]` frame. OpenAPI 3.1 has no vocabulary for "a stream of this shape" -- this is stated in prose rather than modelled as a false single-object response.

post.summary: Score documents against a query with a cross-encoder, most relevant first.
post.description: `documents[].index` in the response is ALWAYS the position the document held in YOUR `documents` array, never the position in the sorted result -- look a scored document back up by that index, not by counting through the response. Omit `top_n` to get every document scored; set it to get only the top N. Set `return_documents: true` to have each result echo its own document text back (otherwise only the index and score are returned). Supports an optional `Idempotency-Key` header, same replay/conflict/body-mismatch contract as `/openai/v1/chat/completions` (see that endpoint's own description).

parameters.description: Only models or only hardware requests. Other: `400`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, lowered to 200. Not a whole number: `400` (`invalid_limit`).

post.summary: Request a model for the board, or vote on the existing request.
post.description: A signed-in browser session only: an API key is refused, as is an operator viewing as an account. Body is `{ "hf_id": "owner/name", "note"?: string }`, or `{ "kind": "hardware", "hardware_class": "H100", "note"?: string }` for a hardware class from the /earn catalog (anything else: 400 `invalid_hardware_class`). `note` plain text of at most 280 characters. A new request answers 201; one that already exists is not duplicated and answers 200 with the existing request. Rate limited per account (429 `model_request_rate_limited`); 413 `request_too_large`.

get.summary: Model deprecations, successors and scheduled price changes.
get.description: Public and anonymous, CORS-open, derived from the same rows as `GET /openai/v1/pricing` so the two cannot disagree. `scheduled` lists models with a future sunset date, `completed` those retired within the last year, `price_changes` every pending price change with its effective time. Every `*_price*` field is micro-dollars per million tokens (`price_unit`). `price_increase_notice_hours` is the enforced minimum notice before an increase takes effect.

get.summary: Past platform price changes, newest first.
get.description: Public and anonymous, CORS-open. DEFAULT OFF: until the operator sets `PRICING_HISTORY_FEED_ENABLED` to `1` or `true` every call answers 404 `not_found`. Already-effective platform list-rate changes only (future ones are in `GET /openai/v1/models/lifecycle`); `*_price_*` fields are micro-dollars per million tokens. Changes before `coverage.since` are not recorded. Page with `next_cursor` unchanged (bad cursor: 400 `invalid_cursor`); `limit` default 100, max 500; `order` `desc` (default) or `asc`.

get.summary: Read a published agent's card by slug.
get.description: Any signed-in account; there is no anonymous read and no guest lane. Dark by default: every public-agent route answers 404 `not_found` unless the deployment enables public agents. Returns the card only: never the system prompt, guardrails or the owner's account id. The visitor's chat rides the `agent_id` field on the visitor's own account, so the visitor pays and the owner is never charged. An unknown or malformed slug is 404. Every response carries `x-robots-tag: noindex`.

post.summary: Diff, and optionally apply, a new version of an imported spec.
post.description: Accepts a key-management credential (not a read-only key). Without `apply: true` nothing is stored and the response only reports what would change; with it the tool set is replaced and the stored spec is returned under `spec`. Per-tool policies survive for tools that remain. Body limit applies (413 `request_too_large`); `servers[0].url` is re-checked (422 `server_url_refused`); a bad `operationId` is 422 `invalid_operation_id`. Unknown or foreign id: 404 `openapi_spec_not_found`.

patch.summary: Set the approval policy of imported tools.
patch.description: Accepts a key-management credential (not a read-only key). Body maps operation names to one of `allow_always`, `require_approval`, `block_always`, `block_in_sensitive_context` (1 to 64 entries); tools not named keep their policy. An operation the spec does not have is 422 `unknown_operation`. Unknown or foreign id: 404 `openapi_spec_not_found`.

post.summary: Mint a single-use setup-script link for a coding client.
post.description: Accepts a key-management credential (not a read-only key). Off by default: the connect surface is absent unless the deployment enables it. Body is exactly `{ "client":... }` where client is one of `claude-code`, `cursor`, `codex`, `aider`. The response `path` is the single-use `GET /connect/script/{token}` link; it expires after `expires_in_s` seconds and the token is never logged. 413 `request_too_large`, 400 `invalid_request`.

get.summary: Redeem a setup link and download its shell script.
get.description: Off by default: this route answers 404 unless the deployment enables the connect surface. Anonymous: the single-use token in the path is the credential, shown once by `POST /openai/v1/connect/setup-links`. Success is `200 text/x-shellscript` with the client's setup script; `404 setup_link_not_found` for an unknown or malformed token, `410 setup_link_gone` once used or expired, `503 base_url_unconfigured`, and a per-IP and aggregate rate limit with `Retry-After`. Always `cache-control: no-store`. This route lives at the host root, not under `/openai/v1`.

200.description: Redeem a setup link and download its shell script. The setup script for the client the link was minted for, as plain text.

get.summary: Git smart-HTTP ref advertisement for your enabled skills.
get.description: Your enabled skills as a READ-ONLY git repository: `git clone https://x:<api-key>@<host>/openai/v1/skills.git`. Only `?service=git-upload-pack` is served (any other service, and dumb HTTP, is 403). A git client sends the key as the Basic-auth password; a missing, unknown or revoked key is 401 with a Basic challenge. The account comes only from the key. Rate limited per account per minute (a clone is two requests).

200.description: Git smart-HTTP ref advertisement for your enabled skills. The git smart-HTTP ref advertisement (pkt-lines) naming this account's single skills commit.

401.description: A missing, unknown or revoked key: `text/plain` (`authentication required`) with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="skills"`. Not the JSON envelope.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Basic realm="skills"`: send the API key as the Basic-auth password.

default.description: Refusal as `text/plain` (403 for a non-upload-pack service, 413/503 for size or availability, 429 with `Retry-After`). Only the 405 above is the JSON envelope.

post.summary: Git smart-HTTP pack download for your enabled skills.
post.description: The git-upload-pack request (`application/x-git-upload-pack-request`, optionally gzip). Every `want` must be your own account's commit; anything else is 400. Request body and pack size are capped (413, 503). Same Basic-password key auth and rate limit as `info/refs`.

git upload-pack request (binary pkt-lines)

200.description: Git smart-HTTP pack download for your enabled skills. The git pack (a `NAK` pkt-line followed by the packfile) for this account's skills commit.

401.description: A missing, unknown or revoked key: `text/plain` (`authentication required`) with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="skills"`. Not the JSON envelope.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Basic realm="skills"`: send the API key as the Basic-auth password.

get.summary: List the published MCP server catalog.
get.description: Public and unauthenticated, same posture as the model catalog. Only `published` global entries are listed. Query: `limit` (1-100, default 20) and `offset`. `?scope=org` instead lists your own organizations' private entries and requires any valid API key.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, lowered to 100. Not a whole number: `400` (`invalid_limit`).

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `org`: your organizations' private entries (needs a key). Other: `422` (`invalid_scope`).

post.summary: Create a draft MCP catalog entry.
post.description: Requires an API key scoped `mcp-catalog:manage` (operator-issued). New entries land as `draft` and are invisible to the public reads until published; `publisher_pubkey` and `attestation_sig` are both-or-neither and are required (and re-verified) before an entry can publish. A duplicate name is a 409 (`name_conflict`). Body limit applies (413 `request_too_large`).

curl-0.value:
curl -X POST https://dicompute.ai/openai/v1/mcp-catalog \
  -H "authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"acme-files","description":"Acme file tools","publisher":"Acme","transport_type":"remote-http","transport_config":"https://mcp.acme.example","version":"1.0.0"}'

get.summary: Read one published MCP catalog entry.
get.description: Public and unauthenticated. A `draft`, `pending_review` or `denied` entry is a 404 (`entry_not_found`), exactly like an id that never existed; `delisted` and `revoked` are a 410 (`entry_delisted` / `entry_revoked`) because the entry's prior existence is not a secret. An organization-private entry is visible only to that organization's members.

patch.summary: Update, publish or delist an MCP catalog entry.
patch.description: Requires an API key scoped `mcp-catalog:manage`. `status` moves through the entry lifecycle (`published` requires the publisher attestation and an operator `review_state: "verified"` set by a different account than the submitter); a published entry is immutable (`published_immutable`). Unknown id is a 404.

delete.description: Requires an API key scoped `mcp-catalog:manage`. Unknown id is a 404 (`entry_not_found`).
